deals.t: Back Bay: Related Beal and Freeport Equity bought the Motor Mart Garage from CIM Group, reportedly for about $89M (CIM paid $162.5M in 2016).
Greater Boston: Investcorp bought an eight-building industrial portfolio for $76.5M.
Chelsea: Flatiron Energy closed about $850M of financing for the 1,200 MWh Energizar battery storage project.

items.t: September CPI came in at 3.7% y/y vs. 3.6% expected, and PPI rose 1.3% in the month to 6.3% y/y, the biggest monthly jump since 2022.
The 10-year closed at 5.10% on Oct 15 and was about 5.09% Friday afternoon, roughly 14 bp lower on the week. The 30-year was about 5.43%.
Prediction markets put an Oct 28 hike at about 14% on Friday, down from 29% on Wednesday; a December hike is still priced near 77%.
Freddie Mac's 30-year held at 7.40%, ending a seven-week run of increases; Mortgage News Daily's index eased to 7.37% on Oct 16.
Boston's BPDA approved tax agreements for four projects totaling about 1,400 apartments, and Manchester's revaluation lifted citywide values 48%, with apartment buildings up the most.

next.t: EIA weekly gasoline and diesel prices: shows whether Brent's Friday rebound to about $109.57 is reaching the pump; New England diesel was $6.441.
September housing starts: consensus 1.310M annual pace, a read on new supply with mortgages at 7.40%.
$13B 20-year bond auction: the next test of demand for long Treasuries.
$26B 5-year TIPS auction and the Freddie Mac mortgage survey: inflation expectations after hot CPI and PPI, and whether mortgage rates turn lower.

2026-10-16.summary: Hot inflation data dominated the week: September CPI rose 3.7% from a year earlier and PPI jumped 6.3%, led by fuel. Long Treasury yields still fell, with the 10-year down about 14 bp to roughly 5.09%, and odds of an October Fed hike dropped to about 14% while a December hike stays near 77%. For Boston and NH real estate, borrowing costs eased slightly but remain high, the 30-year mortgage held at 7.40%, and energy-driven cost pressure on construction and operations continues.

deals.t: Quincy: FoxRock Properties bought 1100 Crown Colony Drive, a 132,000 SF office building, from W.P. Carey for $5.5M; W.P. Carey paid $25.5M in 2013.
Somerville: the three-building, 120-unit Kingsley Orchard portfolio in Davis Square sold for $39M.
Wrentham: BGO bought a fully leased 132,055 SF warehouse at 545 Washington St for $34.9M.

items.h: Biggest bond rally in two years
items.t: The 10-year fell 17 bp to 4.96% on Oct 22, its first close under 5% since Sept 22, as the Nasdaq dropped 2.6% on AI-spending doubts; it was about 4.99% Friday afternoon.
Brent settled at $116.72 on Oct 23, up 3.4% on the day and its third straight weekly gain, on reports of plans for renewed strikes on Iran.
The high-yield spread jumped to 340 bp on Oct 22 from 327 bp, the IG spread rose to 89 bp, and more than $5B of October debt sales were postponed.

items.h: Fed hike bets ease a little
items.t: October hike odds fell to about 8% from about 13% on Oct 20; a December hike is still about 72% likely on Kalshi.
Freddie Mac's 30-year fell to 7.32% from 7.40%, its first drop in eight weeks, and Mortgage News Daily's index was 7.30% on Oct 22.

next.t: $69B 2-year note auction and EIA weekly fuel prices: the first test of demand after the rally, and whether $116 Brent is reaching the pump.
$70B 5-year note auction and a long-bond buyback of at least $4B.
Fed decision: about 8% hike odds; a $28B 2-year FRN sells the same morning.
Q3 GDP, September PCE inflation, $44B of 7-year notes and the Freddie Mac mortgage survey.

2026-10-23.summary: Bonds rallied hard this week: the 10-year fell 17 bp to 4.96% on Oct 22, its biggest one-day drop in more than two years, as an AI-spending selloff hit tech stocks, and it was near 4.99% on Friday afternoon, about 10 bp below last Friday. Brent climbed to $116.72 on Iran strike fears, credit spreads widened and a December Fed hike is still priced at about 72%. For Boston and NH real estate, lower Treasury yields and a 7.32% mortgage rate help at the margin, but wider spreads, rising energy costs and a Quincy office sale 78% below its 2013 price show financing and office values remain under strain.

deals.t: Rockpoint bought back 100 Summer St. at a foreclosure auction for $260M, about $236/SF and 68% below its 2019 price.
EOS Investors bought the 163-room Hyatt Centric Faneuil Hall for $58.4M.
Alexandria agreed to sell its unfinished 421 Park Drive lab tower in the Fenway; the buyer takes on about $136M of interior work.

items.h: Fed holds with two hike dissents
items.t: The Fed kept its range at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote on Oct 28; Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack wanted a quarter-point hike.

items.h: Tech rout drives a Treasury rally
items.t: Intel fell about 30% and the Nasdaq about 3% on Friday after Alphabet's 12% drop on Thursday; the 10-year touched about 4.89%, its lowest since Sept 10.

items.h: Inflation in line, growth strong, wages cooling
items.t: September PCE rose 3.6% and core 3.1%, Q3 GDP grew 3.4%, and private wages rose 3.1% over the year in Q3, the slowest since 2021.
Freddie Mac's 30-year fell to 7.24% from 7.32%, the lowest this month but 107 bp above a year ago.
$211B of 2-, 5- and 7-year Treasury notes and FRNs sold smoothly, Microsoft's $25B bond sale drew $115B of orders, and the high-yield spread ended Thursday at 326 bp.

next.t: Treasury borrowing estimates (3:00 PM ET); EIA fuel prices
Election Day in MA and NH; JOLTS job openings
Treasury quarterly refunding sets November auction sizes

2026-10-30.summary: The Fed held rates at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 with two officials voting for a hike, but weak results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel sent tech stocks sharply lower on Thursday and Friday and pushed money into Treasuries. The 10-year fell to about 4.93% on Friday afternoon from 5.00% last Friday, capping an October drop of about 36 bp, while December hike odds slipped to about 72% from a peak of 79%. For Boston and New Hampshire owners, fixed-rate borrowing costs are lower than a month ago, floating-rate debt still faces a likely December hike, and downtown office distress is now trading at deep discounts.

changes.t: Down from $113.43 last Friday, with a low of $94.62 on Nov 4 amid hopes for an easing of the conflict with Iran.
Thursday's AI-stock rout cut the Nasdaq 5.5% in a day; Friday recovered only part of it.
Since last Friday's 4.94%; it touched 4.84% on Nov 5, its lowest close since Sep 9.
It dropped as low as 4.46% on Nov 5 before the jobs report pushed it back up.
Far above forecasts near 60,000; unemployment fell to 4.1%.
Up from about 72% a week earlier, after swinging between 80% on Nov 4 and 69% on Nov 5.
Down from 7.24%, a third straight weekly decline.
Up from 344 bp last Friday after swinging to 332 bp on Nov 4 (Nov 5 reading).

deals.t: Bulfinch Companies bought 210 Broadway in Cambridge from BioMed Realty for $15.1M, about $233/SF.
Planning Office for Urban Affairs and JGE Development bought a 1.6-acre Mattapan garage site for $8.75M for 105 income-restricted units.

2026-11-06.headline: AI-stock rout and strong jobs data leave the 10-year 8 bp lower

items.t: Democrats won the House and Senate; markets rallied on Wednesday before an AI-stock rout on Thursday tied partly to fears of tighter AI rules.
The Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 4.4% on Nov 5, and the 10-year fell to 4.84%, its lowest close since Sep 9.
October payrolls rose 165,000 and December hike odds climbed to 77% from 69%.
Brent fell to $98.32 from $113.43 last Friday.
Massachusetts voters rejected Question 7 by about 1.2 points.

next.t: October CPI (8:30 AM ET); $42B 10-year note auction
Bond market closed (Veterans Day); stocks open

items.t: Treasury kept the 3-, 10- and 30-year sizes and dropped "at least" from its guidance on steady sizes.
Oct–Dec was trimmed to $618B.
The dollar deal drew about $58B of orders and the euro debut about €53B.
About $31B of orders on Nov 5.
Payrolls rose 165,000 in October and unemployment fell to 4.1%.
Voters rejected smaller-lot starter homes by about 1.2 points.
Healey and Ayotte were reelected, and Chris Pappas won New Hampshire's Senate seat.
About $233/SF for 64,812 SF; BioMed Realty paid $23.5M in 2012.
Approved for 105 income-restricted units.
September JOLTS beat the 7.10M forecast.
Unemployment 4.1%, wages +3.1% over the year.

items.h: Data center suppliers hit hardest on Thursday
items.t: AMD fell 17.3%, Micron about 17.5%, IREN 17%, Dell 15%, Nebius 14.9%, Vertiv 14.1%, Quanta 12.3% and Nvidia 9.3%, on fears the new Congress could slow AI data center construction. Microsoft (−3.6%), Amazon (−2.2%) and Google (−1.9%) held up best. Banks, investment banks and alternative asset managers also fell.
CoreWeave's debt has repriced from about a 9% yield to 15% in recent weeks. Oracle began raising about $10B in debt and equity for data centers, and its stock fell 9% on Monday.
Third-quarter free cash flow was about −$9B at Alphabet and −$33B at Amazon, as AI spending outran operating cash.
Search revenue grew 12%, down from 19% in the first quarter of 2026.

Third-quarter revenue grew 47% from the second quarter, down from 147%, and revenue fell to 1.72× compute costs from 2.08×. The filing lists about $895B of lease and other AI commitments. Token prices were cut by up to 50% in October, and the IPO is expected within weeks.

items.h: AI suppliers still report strong quarters
items.t: AMD revenue rose 45% to $13.38B, with about $17B guided for Q4. Arista rose 58% to $3.7B, Palantir 96% to $2.3B, and Eaton 28% to $8.95B with raised guidance.

Booking's revenue slipped to $8.89B from $9.01B, with Q4 growth guided at 0–2%. Apple's services growth slowed to 10%, and Qualcomm's handset chip sales fell 26% as memory prices hit phone sales. FIS fell 24% after pausing buybacks, cutting guidance and losing its CFO.
For only the third time in its history, FICO gave no annual outlook, citing competition from VantageScore in mortgage credit scoring.
Spread-related earnings rose only 7% as it took a conservative approach to new credit. Apollo is now one of the largest lenders to AI data centers, and its stock is down 19% this year.

2026-11-06.summary: Democrats won Congress, an AI-stock rout sent the Nasdaq down 5.5% on Thursday, and a strong October jobs report on Friday lifted December hike odds to 77%. Treasuries still rallied for the week, with the 10-year down 8 bp to 4.86% and Brent down to $98.32 from $113.43. For Boston and New Hampshire owners, fixed-rate borrowing costs are near their lowest since early September, but a likely December hike keeps floating-rate debt under pressure and wider junk spreads signal more cautious lenders.
